1.title: Ingesting Data (2): Syslog and CEF, Azure Activity, Threat Indicators and Custom Tables
1.text: Welcome to Module eight: Ingesting Data (two): sys log and C E F, Azure Activity, Threat Indicators and Custom Tables. It covers the exam area one. Manage a security operations environment. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Plan and configure sys log via A M A and Common Event Format (C E F) via A M A connectors. Configure collection of Azure activity logs by using Azure Policy and resource diagnostic settings. Ingest threat indicators into Microsoft Sentinel. Create custom log tables in the workspace to store ingested data. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one. Manage a security operations environment (forty to forty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: Syslog and CEF via AMA
1.text: sys log and C E F via A M A. The figure shows this: A log forwarder receives sys log or C E F and A M A sends it to the workspace.

1.title: Syslog and CEF via AMA, continued
1.text: sys log and C E F via A M A. Network devices, firewalls and Linux hosts send sys log or Common Event Format (C E F) messages. A Linux log forwarder receives them and the Azure Monitor Agent sends them to the workspace. Table. sys log via A M A: sys log. C E F via A M A: Common Security Log. Message. sys log via A M A: Standard sys log. C E F via A M A: sys log with C E F fields (vendor, product, severity). Install first. sys log via A M A: The matching Content hub solution. C E F via A M A: The matching Content hub solution.

1.title: Syslog and CEF via AMA, continued
1.text: sys log and C E F via A M A. Software. A Linux V M running R sys log or sys log N G; Python two point seven or three required. Non-Azure forwarder. Needs Azure Arc (Connected Machine agent). Ports. The daemon listens on U D P and T C P five hundred fourteen; A M A one point two eight.eleven or later receives from the daemon on T C P twenty-eight thousand three hundred thirty. Roles. Virtual Machine Contributor or Azure Connected Machine Resource Administrator to deploy; Monitoring Contributor for the D C R.

1.title: Syslog and CEF via AMA, continued
1.text: sys log and C E F via A M A. Facility and severity in the D C R: you choose a minimum level per facility; Sentinel collects that level and all higher severities (L O G E R R collects E R R, C R I T, A L E R T, E M E R G). The portal sets only a minimum; the A P I can list exact levels. Exam tip: Same facility in both a sys log and a C E F rule duplicates events across the two tables. Fix it at the source or with a K Q L filter in the D C R. Validate with netstat -lnptv (port five hundred fourteen), tcpdump, or a K Q L query on Common Security Log. Data can take up to twenty minutes to appear.

1.title: Azure activity logs
1.text: Azure activity logs. The Azure Activity log records subscription-level operations. Table: Azure Activity. It uses the diagnostic settings pipeline. Azure Policy (a policy that deploys a diagnostic setting to send logs to the workspace). Many subscriptions or resources at scale; assigned at a management group or subscription. Diagnostic settings on one resource: resource, then Diagnostic settings, then plus Add diagnostic setting, then Send to Log Analytics workspace. One resource.

1.title: Azure activity logs, continued
1.text: Azure activity logs. Basics. Scope. Parameters. Uncheck Only show parameters that require input; choose the workspace. Remediation. Create a remediation task so existing resources are configured too. The policy effect is Deploy If Not Exists. You need Owner on the policy assignment scope. A policy-managed connector shows Connected only if data arrived in the past fourteen days. Subscriptions connected by the legacy method must be disconnected first (Disconnect All). Some resources write to Azure Diagnostics, others to resource-specific tables. Exam tip: Policy equals scale. Remediation task equals existing resources. A new policy assignment alone only affects new resources.

1.title: Threat intelligence
1.text: Threat intelligence. Threat intelligence arrives as indicators of compromise (Io Cs), such as I P s, domains, U R Ls and file hashes. Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence connector. Standard and premium (premium adds Microsoft I O Cs and enriched oh sint). Threat Intelligence - taxi. Imports taxi two point zero and two point one feeds: friendly name, A P I root U R L, collection I D, username and password, polling frequency. Upload A P I (preview). An Entra app with Microsoft Sentinel Contributor at workspace level; client I D, oh auth token, workspace I D. Threat Intelligence Platform connector. Deprecated (Graph ti Indicators A P I). Bulk import. Flat file (C S V or Jason) in the threat intelligence page.

1.title: Threat intelligence, continued
1.text: Threat intelligence. Tables. Threat Intel Indicators and Threat Intel Objects (S T I X-based); the legacy Threat Intelligence Indicator stopped ingesting after July thirty-one, twenty twenty-five. sticks objects. Threat actor, Attack pattern, Indicator, Identity, Relationship. T L P. White, Green, Amber, Red. Refresh. Indicators are re-ingested every seven to ten days and de-duplicated. Manage. Defender portal Threat intelligence page (Intel management). Use. Rule templates named T I map... to Microsoft Sentinel; hourly run, one-hour lookback by default, alert when results greater than zero; lookback up to fourteen days. Microsoft Threat Intelligence Analytics is a rule that cannot be customized; it matches C E F, sys log and Windows D N S events against domain, I P and U R L indicators. Exam tip: taxi needs the A P I root and the collection I D. New tables: Threat Intel Indicators and Threat Intel Objects.

2.title: Custom log tables
2.text: Custom log tables. A custom table stores data that no built-in connector writes. Name ends with underscore C L. Create. Log Analytics workspace, then Tables, then Create, then New custom log (D C R-based); choose or create a D C R, a data collection endpoint (D C E), upload a sample Jason, optionally add a K Q L transformation. Time Generated. Required; added automatically if missing. Plans. Analytics (default), Basic, Auxiliary or lake. Roles. Log Analytics Contributor (tables); Monitoring Contributor (D C Rs). Delete. Custom tables only; Azure tables cannot be deleted.

2.title: Custom log tables, continued
2.text: Custom log tables. Logs Ingestion A P I: an app registration (with secret) posts Jason to the D C E or D C R endpoint; the D C R needs Monitoring Metrics Publisher for the app. The stream name is Custom- followed by the table name ending in underscore C L, the token scope is https: or or monitor.azure.com, and the transform Kql source passes data unchanged. Exam tip: Custom table equals underscore C L suffix, a D C R, a D C E and Time Generated. The ingestion app gets Monitoring Metrics Publisher on the D C R.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A firewall sends C E F messages to a Linux V M running R sys log. Which connector and table should the sock use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: C E F via A M A, with events stored in the Common Security Log table. C E F messages are collected by C E F via A M A into Common Security Log.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. The same firewall messages appear in both the sys log and Common Security Log tables. What is the usual cause and fix? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The same facility is used in both rules; fix it at the source or filter in the D C R. Sending the same facility to sys log and C E F duplicates rows, so fix it at the source or with a D C R K Q L filter.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. An organization with two hundred subscriptions needs the Azure Activity log in Sentinel, including subscriptions that already exist. What is the best approach? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Assign an Azure Policy at the management group and create a remediation task. Policy scales across subscriptions and a remediation task configures existing ones.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A partner shares indicators from a taxi two point one server. Which information is needed in the taxi connector? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The A P I root U R L and the collection I D of the feed. The taxi connector needs the A P I root U R L and collection I D, and a username and password if the feed requires them.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. An analyst wants to query the current S T I X-based indicators in Sentinel. Which tables hold them? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Threat Intel Indicators and Threat Intel Objects, the new tables. The new schema writes indicators to Threat Intel Indicators and Threat Intel Objects; the legacy table stopped after July thirty-one, twenty twenty-five.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. An application posts Jason to a custom table through the Logs Ingestion A P I. Which role must the app registration hold on the D C R? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Monitoring Metrics Publisher, to send data. The app needs Monitoring Metrics Publisher on the D C R to send data.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which table receives C E F data? Answer: Common Security Log. Question two. Which port does the forwarder daemon listen on? Answer: U D P and T C P five hundred fourteen. Question three. Which policy effect configures diagnostic settings automatically? Answer: Deploy If Not Exists.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What suffix does a custom table have? Answer: underscore C L. Question five. What does a remediation task do? Answer: Applies the policy to existing resources. Question six. Which legacy indicator table stopped ingesting after July thirty-one, twenty twenty-five? Answer: Threat Intelligence Indicator.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. sys log and C E F: Linux forwarder, R sys log or sys log N G, port five hundred fourteen; tables sys log and Common Security Log. Severity: minimum level per facility collects that level and higher. Azure Activity: Azure Activity table; Azure Policy at scale plus remediation task. Threat intelligence: taxi (A P I root, collection I D), Upload A P I, new tables Threat Intel Indicators and Threat Intel Objects. Custom tables: underscore C L, D C R, D C E, Time Generated; Monitoring Metrics Publisher for ingestion apps.
